newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen steady in volatile triple-witching.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen steady in volatile triple-witching.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open steady despite today's volatile "triple-witching" expiration of options and futures on shares and share indices, which generates massive turnover at the beginning and end of the trading session.
"It should be a very volatile session, but I expect it to go slightly to the upside," said Westfalia Investments director of research Peter Cardillo.
The absence of any real economic data and the upcoming meeting of the Federal Reserve would keep bonds on hold and stocks in check, limiting any major gains, he said.
"Triple-witching has really become kind of tame," said Larry Wachtel, Prudential Securities market analyst.

The expiry is likely to add to opening and closing volumes, he said, but "in betweeen it should be quiet. I don't see much change ... We'll have the same lassitude we've been seeing all week ahead of the Fed meeting."
The U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday, and may take evidence of strong U.S. economic growth as a prompt to raise interest rates by about a quarter percentage point.
